SHALLOWEST/BIGGEST FINDING: describeCapability's own guidance for this route explicitly claims the response's test_cases rows come from 'a different serializer from the run's case LISTING... kept separate so corrections to the listing shape do not silently redescribe this one', and declares a narrow item shape (identifier, name, description, priority as a string label, status as a string, case_type, latest_status, latest_result_id, assignee as a string, folder_path as int array, configuration_id, dataset, project_id as 'PR-1' string, source_project_id as 'PR-7' string). The ACTUAL response is not that shape at all — it is the exact same wide row shape list_test_run_test_cases_by_integer_id returns (assignee/priority/case_type/automation_state as full objects, mapping_id instead of latest_result_id, configuration instead of configuration_id, test_case_folders_path instead of folder_path, no source_project_id, project_id as a bare integer not 'PR-NNN'). The 'kept separate' claim in the guidance is false: this is the listing shape, unmodified. Confirmed on both writes in this probe (identical item shape both times).

WHAT IT ACTUALLY EDITS — CONFIRMED EMPIRICALLY: after the write, get_test_case_by_integer_id on TC-54485 (1985019) showed the case's OWN record completely untouched by this call — description still read the leftover text from an unrelated prior probe ('PARTIAL-EDIT PROBE: single-field update via edit_test_case_partial...'), status still 'Active' (id 318632), updated_at still 2026-09-21T13:42:43.000Z (a full 16 hours before this probe's write at 05:38:20 the next day). Meanwhile the SAME call correctly set the run row's latest_status to 'blocked' and minted a new result (id 2150424086). This capability writes execution results scoped to a run row, never the case's own fields — the guidance's own claim on this point holds up under test, and the misleading part is purely the response-shape claim above, not the write-scope claim.

STATUS-ID INCONSISTENCY — CONFIRMED, SAME RESULT ROW, TWO READERS DISAGREE: sent status_id=318612 (resolved from get_test_runs_form_fields as 'Blocked'). list_test_run_test_cases_by_integer_id's re-read of the same row echoes result_status.id=318612 (matches what was sent). But list_test_results_for_test_case_by_integer_id, reading the identical result row (id 2150424086) by its own dedicated per-result read, reports result_status.id=318639 for the SAME field_value 'Blocked' / internal_name 'blocked' / colour '#818CF8'. Same fact, same instant, two callers, two different numeric ids for the same status — reproducing exactly the 318612-vs-318639 pattern flagged elsewhere in this campaign, now confirmed on this capability's own write and a sibling read of the row it just created.

DUPLICATE-ROW CHECK — NEGATIVE, NOTABLE: re-read TR-9120's row count via list_test_run_test_cases_by_integer_id immediately after the first write (5 cases in, 5 rows out, info.count:5) and again after the second write (still 5 rows, info.count:5). The create_step_result duplicate-row defect (one call producing two case-level result rows) does NOT reproduce on this capability across two separate writes — a genuine, useful negative result for this specific route.

SILENT PARTIAL FAILURE — CONFIRMED, NO SIGNAL AT ALL: a second write sent mapping_ids:[2150424067 (valid, TC-54456), 999999999 (nonexistent)] with status_id=318611 (Failed). Response: 200, success:true, skipped_test_case_ids: [] (empty — not populated for a bad mapping_id, only for review-gate exclusions per its own doc), the valid row (TC-54456) correctly updated to Failed, and absolutely no field anywhere in the response indicating that one of the two requested mapping_ids matched nothing. This is a fourth distinct partial-failure behavior in this bulk-route family (alongside create_bulk_test_cases's silent-discard-200, edit_test_run/list_test_run_test_cases_by_integer_id's named-skip, and bulk_set_test_case_assignee_in_run's all-or-nothing-502): silent-no-op-200-with-zero-signal. An agent cannot tell from this response alone whether N or N-1 (or fewer) of its requested mapping_ids actually applied.
